sam (newbie): Hey — running the docker quickstart. First API call returns 403 with body 'workspace_limited'. I set REDWOOD_API_KEY via docker -e but still failing.

marta (devex): Welcome! Which quickstart & SDK version? Quick starts sometimes have mismatched env names between .env.example and the entrypoint.

sam (newbie): Using examples/node/docker, image built from main. Command: `docker run -e REDWOOD_API_KEY=$KEY redwood/quickstart`
Response: `{"error":"workspace_limited","message":"workspace has limited access"}`

leo (sdk-eng): Two things to check: 1) confirm the env is present inside the container (`docker exec -it <id> env | grep REDWOOD`), and 2) check org billing state. We recently tightened SDK behavior so missing keys don't silently fallback.

sam (newbie): env shows REDWOOD_API_KEY set.

marta (devex): Hmm. I can check billing for your org if you share the org id privately. Sometimes the onboarding SSO flow leaves billing in a partial state (modal closed).

billing-bot: Auto: Retrieved org redwood-sam-test — status: "Limited: payment info required". Certain endpoints blocked until payment info or dev-unlock.

sam (newbie): Ah — I closed the SSO/billing modal earlier. Didn't realize that left it limited.

leo (sdk-eng): We'll improve the quickstart to detect the workspace_limited response and print a clear next step. For now, either finish billing in console or request a short dev unlock from billing.

marta (devex): Filed quickstart docs PR to call out SSO/billing modal and env variable checks. Also adding a tiny note in README: "If you see workspace_limited, check billing & SSO modal."

billing-bot: Auto: Created ticket BILL-4029 and notified payments team for manual dev unlock option.

sam (newbie): I finished the billing step and retried — first call now succeeds. Thanks all!
